title: Facilities, Buildings & Grounds Stewardship for Inspection Station Networks
capability_statement: Parsons brings the program-management depth of an $80-year, $5.4B-annual-revenue engineering and operations firm with 18,000+ employees and a vehicle inspection compliance division of more than 500 professionals available regionally to take operational responsibility for the buildings, grounds, and on-site equipment supporting an inspection-facility portfolio. Across our concurrent state and provincial inspection programs (PennDOT, Vermont DMV, Hawaii DOT, Texas DPS, Ontario MOECC, and the existing Northeast hybrid I/M program) we already coordinate station-level facility access, security sign-in/sign-out, on-site equipment deployment, software certification, ATP-driven equipment testing, building maintenance, and field-service dispatch across thousands of inspection lanes. Beyond inspection facilities, Parsons holds large active vehicles for hands-on facility design, construction, and maintenance work that directly map to the trade scope of this RFP: the U.S. Air Force Comprehensive Construction & Engineering MATOC ($15B ceiling, 5-year base + 5 option years for global facility design, construction management, maintenance, renovation, and restoration), the Pacific Deterrence Initiative MACC NAVFAC IDIQ ($15B ceiling for design and engineering of runways, hangars, waterfront facilities, and energy/fuel storage), the MDA Real Property Program ($104.2M for facility restoration/modernization), the AFCEC Environmental Services Contract for PFAS ($1.5B ceiling), the McMurdo Station (Antarctica) update and rebuild, and the $100M Nammo munitions-facility design/construction task order. Our regional office structure (currently three I/M regional offices plus centralized headquarters and full remote-work capability proven during COVID-19) provides the dispatch-and-coverage model needed to deliver routine janitorial, grounds-keeping, snow-removal, HVAC, electrical, plumbing, alarm, and structural maintenance on a multi-site portfolio where some sites are wholly contractor-occupied and others are shared. We bring a documented quality-assurance framework, financial-stability profile (publicly traded NYSE:PSN, more than 60 percent owned by the Parsons Employee Stock Ownership Trust, three years of audited financials available) sufficient to fund routine service and maintenance at our own expense and to carry monthly utility, alarm, and rental obligations, and an SCM-style procurement and approval workflow already used for capital decisions, escrow controls, third-party quotes, and proof-of-purchase documentation. Our facility assessment, capital planning, and OEM-aligned preventive-maintenance discipline applied today to inspection equipment translates directly to building-systems planning, the annual master inventory list, and the standardized PM/structural/property-repair Plan required within 180 days of contract effective date. For shared co-located areas we will operate to the SCM-approved scope at no additional charge, hold three independent quotes for remediation work, secure written approval before alterations, and conduct single-lane maintenance outside posted hours so motorist-facing operations are not interrupted.

differentiators: (1) Active multi-billion-dollar federal facility design/construction/maintenance prime vehicles (USAF MATOC, NAVFAC PDI MACC, MDA Real Property Program, AFCEC PFAS) substantially close the v1 gap around hands-on building-trades and environmental-remediation capability and place Parsons in a small group of inspection-program operators that simultaneously hold prime facility-trade contracts. (2) Operating tenure across six concurrent state and provincial inspection programs gives Parsons direct, in-place experience with the access-controlled, sign-in/sign-out, security-protocol environment the RFP requires before any contractor personnel may enter a facility. (3) Demonstrated multi-site mobilization tempo (1,200 Vermont facilities in 6 months; 6,700 Texas stations in 4 months) shows we can stand up the maintenance, janitorial, grounds, and snow-removal coverage matrix on day one of contract performance. (4) Existing OEM-aligned preventive-maintenance discipline for inspection equipment, including ATP scripting, calibration, equipment testing and approval, electronic Inventory Control System with automatic-notification movement tracking, and bill-of-sale/proof-of-ownership controls, directly supports the parallel PM, spare-parts, and equipment-purchase documentation requirements for facility equipment. (5) Three-region operational redundancy (Pittsburgh, Harrisburg, Philadelphia) plus remote-work proven during COVID-19 evidences the dispatch model and continuity needed for snow events, alarm calls, and after-hours single-lane maintenance windows. (6) NJ MVC OSHA VPP recognition at 12 Parsons-operated inspection stations provides third-party validation of housekeeping, hazard-control, and facility-condition standards. (7) Established procurement, escrow (Iron Mountain), and quote-comparison workflows already used on capital decisions translate directly to the three-quote remediation rule, written-approval-before-alteration rule, and SCM-approval workflow for capital repairs and Plan updates. (8) Publicly traded firm with $5.4B+ revenue, 18,000+ employees, and Employee Stock Ownership Trust governance has the balance-sheet depth to carry routine maintenance, alarm fees, utilities, and trailer-rental obligations at Contractor expense without cost recovery. (9) Documented prior-transition commitment to mobilize electricians, construction managers, janitorial resources, and field-service technicians to every station, kiosk, and FIS location prior to go-live shows the trades-and-services taxonomy is already part of Parsons' transition operating model.
gap_notes: While the corporate dossier substantially strengthens the trade-prime story (USAF MATOC, NAVFAC PDI, MDA Real Property, AFCEC PFAS, Nammo, McMurdo), the inspection-program evidence base for this theme still does not directly substantiate every line-item in the Facilities, Buildings & Grounds scope. Capture team must source and attach: (a) for janitorial scope (A-002 carpet steam extraction twice yearly, A-012 HEPA-filter vacuuming, R-101 daily carpet vacuuming) - named janitorial subcontractor or self-perform plan with crew sizing, equipment lists, and HEPA equipment specifications (the dossier confirms janitorial resources are part of Parsons' transition mobilization model but does not provide product-level HEPA spec sheets or daily-frequency scheduling matrices); (b) for grounds-keeping (A-028 monthly rough-lawn mowing of drainage ditches, catch basins, wood lots, transitions) - landscaping subcontractor or self-perform plan including equipment, frequencies, and drainage-area access procedures; (c) for snow removal - while McMurdo Station experience evidences extreme-climate facility operations, no inspection-program-level snow-removal SLA, equipment list, or response-time commitment is in evidence and a teaming partner or named subcontractor with response-time-SLA track record should be identified; (d) for HVAC maintenance per PEOSH (A-086) - the USAF MATOC and NAVFAC PDI MACC establish federal-standard facility maintenance prime capacity, but a PEOSH-specific compliance approach (Public Employees Occupational Safety and Health) at the inspection-station level is not in evidence and should be drafted with explicit PEOSH cross-reference; (e) for the standardized PM/structural-repair/property-repair Plan (A-072, due within 180 days of contract effective date) - no template Plan from a prior project is in evidence and one should be drafted from the USAF/NAVFAC/MDA precedents; (f) for the annual master inventory list (A-034) - no example deliverable is in evidence and the format/scope must be developed (the electronic Inventory Control System chunks describe parts-and-equipment tracking but not the facility-master-list deliverable); (g) for energy-efficient lighting/appliance replacement (A-053, EO 54 / N.J.S.A. 52:34-6.4) - no statute-specific compliance approach is in evidence and a state-jurisdiction reference will be needed; (h) for the Randolph Service Core trailer (M-030, ~$300/month) - the Parsons evidence does not address trailer leasing or hookup-cost handling and capture team must confirm whether the existing trailer will be assumed, replaced, or relocated; (i) for shared co-located area repairs at no additional charge (A-095, R-002) - while Parsons has the financial capacity to absorb such costs and the federal facility prime contracts evidence multi-tenant facility delivery, no past-performance example of repeated no-charge shared-area work is in evidence and a teaming case study should be sought; (j) for the historical Appendix 3.2G capital-expenditure baseline (R-004, M-048) - capture team must obtain Appendix 3.2G itself and incorporate the historical FY2009 to FY2024 spend ranges into pricing assumptions; (k) for facility regulations/security-protocol observance (R-047, R-056) - while Parsons' on-site operations show repeated state-facility access experience, the specific MVC sign-in/sign-out and security-protocol procedures must be captured and documented; (l) for site-specific lighting-level adequacy testing (A-091) - no methodology in evidence; (m) past performance evidence references multiple jurisdictions by name; in the Solution Catalog these descriptions stand as separate prior projects, but any narrative re-used in a new-state-specific proposal must keep these as separate prior projects rather than blending them into the current solicitation's voice; (n) the dossier highlights past New Jersey procurement disputes (2016 and 2021/2022 protests of the Enhanced MV Inspection Maintenance System award) - capture team should brief leadership on incumbency-versus-competitor positioning before re-using state-specific proposal language; (o) for installation-level work instructions (R-001 roller-assembly torque, R-004 hex-bolt locking) - documented as work-instruction-level evidence and should be supplemented with a project-level equipment-installation past-performance narrative.
